purpose: A source-controlled catalogue of major religious and philosophical text corpora. It distinguishes complete texts, complete-text external readers, excerpts, and planned research so the atlas never labels a partial source as a whole book.
rules: Name the tradition, work, edition, language, translator and source separately.
A full canonical corpus is not the same thing as a single denomination's canon.
Ancient originals may be public domain while modern translations remain copyrighted.
Use public-domain editions where redistribution is appropriate; otherwise link to the authoritative library rather than copying the translation.
Never treat a modern commentary, summary or excerpt as the primary scripture itself.

texts.source_note: Project Gutenberg eBook 30 identifies the complete KJV as 80 books spanning Old Testament, Apocrypha and New Testament and marks the edition public domain in the USA.
Sefaria identifies the Torah as the Five Books of Moses and provides structured Hebrew and English text access.
Sefaria provides a structured Tanakh library and text API.
Project Gutenberg hosts a complete English translation by J. M. Rodwell. The Arabic Qur'an remains the primary Arabic text; translations are interpretations and should be labeled as such.
Project Gutenberg provides the complete Edwin Arnold English translation, The Song Celestial.

texts.scope: multiple texts; no single universally fixed book list
texts.source_note: The Upanishads form a corpus rather than one universally bounded volume. The atlas therefore models individual texts and editions separately.

texts.work: Dao De Jing / Tao Te Ching
texts.source_note: Wikisource provides the Chinese text alongside a public-domain James Legge translation; the work has 81 chapters.

texts.scope: 423 verses in 26 chapters in the standard Pali recension
texts.source_note: SuttaCentral provides structured access to the Dhammapada and related Buddhist texts.
A corpus rather than one book. The atlas should model Nikayas, Vinaya and Abhidhamma as separate collections and texts.

texts.scope: Life of the Buddha attributed to Ashvaghosha; Sanskrit transmission incomplete
texts.source_note: An important classical Buddha biography. Sanskrit survives incompletely while fuller versions survive in Chinese and Tibetan transmission; individual translations must be identified.
A major Mahayana biographical text describing the Buddha's life through the first sermon; transmission and editions should be tracked separately.
The standard Sri Guru Granth Sahib is organized to 1,430 ang. Reader editions and translations must be labeled separately from the Gurmukhi text.

texts.scope: Yasna, Visperad, Vendidad/Videvdad, Yashts and Khordeh Avesta traditions
texts.source_note: The Avesta is a corpus with multiple textual strata, not one uniform book. The atlas should preserve that structure.

texts.scope: central book of laws and ordinances
texts.source_note: Use the official Baha'i Library for authoritative text and translation rather than copying a modern edition into the repository.
Chinese Text Project provides the classical Chinese text and translation resources.
The received Zhuangzi contains 33 chapters; the Inner Chapters and later layers should be distinguished in metadata.

texts.scope: Digambara and Svetambara traditions have different canonical histories and collections
texts.source_note: Jain scripture is not one universally identical canon across sects; preserve sectarian textual structures instead of flattening them.

texts.scope: foundational classical Japanese chronicles with mythic and historical material
texts.source_note: These are foundational textual sources for Japanese mythology and early religious history, but neither should be treated as a single Shinto Bible.

texts.scope: collection of Old Norse poems preserved principally in medieval manuscripts
texts.source_note: The Poetic Edda is a manuscript corpus rather than a single ancient canonical book; manuscript provenance and translation matter.

texts.scope: collection of hymns to Greek gods
texts.source_note: Use critical editions and translations through established classical-text libraries; treat mythology, ritual and later literary reception as separate layers.

future_layers: Indigenous traditions where reliable primary-source editions exist
